document.title: Usama Bin Ladin: GOP Official - Claiming Taliban Want to Get Rid of Bin Ladin - Reviews Three Options for Dealing With Him (Islama 07553)
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), Mullah Omar Called Washington in 1998, New Documents Show
document.note: [Secret (NODIS)] A Pakistani official tells Ambassador Milam the Taliban want to rid themselves of bin Laden and lists three options. He emphasizes option two, in which the U.S. would purchase bin Laden from the Taliban for a large sum. The cable also notes Taliban claims that expelling him would get them overthrown because of Pashtun tribal custom. Excised.

persons.name: Usama Bin Ladin
persons.role: Terrorist leader hosted in Taliban-controlled Afghanistan; subject of Taliban/GOP expulsion options

mentions.quote: THE TALIBAN WANTED TO RID THEMSELVES OF BIN LADIN BECAUSE HE WAS A PROBLEM FOR THEM.
MULLAH JALIL HAD REFERRED TO BIN LADIN AS "AN ENEMY."
BIN LADIN, IF CONVICTED, WOULD BE SUMMARILY EXECUTED.
RECENT MERTINGS WHEN TALIBAN LEADER MULLAH OMAR AND "DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER" MULLAH JALIL HAD REFERRED TO BIN LADIN AS "AN ENEMY."
"DEPUTY FOREIGN MINISTER" MULLAH JALIL HAD REFERRED TO BIN LADIN AS "AN ENEMY."
SAID HE HAD A MESSAGE FROM MULLAH JALIL TO THE U.S.
POSSIBLY JALIL HIMSELF, WILL BE COMING TO MEET UN SPECIAL ENVOY BRAHIMI HERE

persons.name: Mullah Hassan
persons.role: Taliban 'Acting Foreign Minister'; proposed head of delegation to Riyadh

mentions.quote: THE DELEGATION WOULD BE HEADED BY "ACTING FOREIGN MINISTER" MULLAH HASSAN
WOULD INCLUDE "ACTING PLANNING MINISTER" QARI DIIN MOHAMMAD, AS WELL AS OTHER IMPORTANT TALIBAN.
CLASSIFIED BY AMBASSADOR WILLIAM B. MILAM.
WILL BE COMING TO MEET UN SPECIAL ENVOY BRAHIMI HERE IN THE NEXT SEVERAL DAYS.

events.description: US Ambassador Milam met a GOP official who claimed the Taliban want to be rid of Bin Ladin and outlined three options.
Mullah Jalil, via the Taliban-controlled embassy, invited a US delegation to Kandahar for talks on 'pending questions'.
US strikes at Khost, after which the US repeatedly told the Taliban it was open to talks.
Russian air crew held by Taliban (1995-6); released after reported $1 million per crew member payment, cited as model for buying out Bin Ladin.
Taliban captured a Russian air crew (1995-6); Russia reportedly bought out the seven-man crew for $1M each.
U.S. strikes on Khost; U.S. has since repeatedly told Taliban it is open to talks.
Ambassador Milam met a GOP official who said the Taliban want to get rid of Bin Ladin and outlined three options.
Mullah Jalil conveyed, via Taliban-controlled embassy phone call, an invitation to a U.S. delegation to visit Kandahar for talks on 'pending questions'.
Embassy requests Department guidance; recommends considering talks in Islamabad or Quetta rather than Kandahar.

key_claims: A GOP official told the US Ambassador that the Taliban want to rid themselves of Bin Ladin.
The Taliban fear being overthrown if they expel Bin Ladin because Pashtun custom requires offering refuge.
Three options: a joint Afghan/Saudi ulema committee, paying the Taliban to expel him, or a Taliban court judging him over Khobar Towers complaints.
The official strongly intimated the buy-out option, citing the Russian air crew ransomed for $1 million each.
Mullah Jalil offered a US delegation visit to Kandahar; the Embassy suggested Islamabad or Quetta as safer venues.
